name: Vanquish ME
lead: Vanquish ME is a hands-free body-contouring system from BTL Industries that uses selective radiofrequency (RF) energy to warm fat tissue and thin the fat layer over the abdomen and thighs.[1][2] People book a short series of clinic sessions to slim the waist and thighs without needles, incisions or an applicator pressed against the skin.

Treatment is non-contact: the energy field is aimed at the target area from a panel held over the body, and the studied abdominal protocol used four weekly 45-minute sessions.[1] The device was developed as a redesigned successor to the original Vanquish, built for more efficient, predictable and even energy delivery to the target tissue.[1]

Published research on the system comes from two 2016 clinical evaluations: a randomised multi-centre comparison with the original Vanquish for abdominal fat thickness, and a clinical evaluation of a selective RF applicator for thigh circumference.[1][2] Both examined the manufacturer's platform.

chain: Selective RF warms subcutaneous fat from a distance
Fat layer thins over a series of weekly sessions
angle.text: Vanquish ME is used in aesthetic clinics as a short course of sessions aimed at a smaller waist and thigh circumference. Because nothing touches the skin and there is no incision, people use it as a non-surgical route to a leaner midsection and legs.

paras: The system delivers radiofrequency energy through a hands-free applicator aimed at the treatment area, so no part of the device contacts the skin and no needles or incisions are involved.[1] Selective RF is designed to act on subcutaneous fat, the layer between the skin and muscle that determines how much the waist and thighs measure.[1][2]
The ME version was described by its evaluators as thoroughly redesigned from the original Vanquish to give more efficient, predictable and homogeneous delivery of energy to the targeted tissue.[1]

In the published abdominal protocol, each participant had four weekly 45-minute treatments, with abdominal fat measured before the first session and again four weeks after the last.[1] A separate evaluation looked at an RF applicator aimed at the thighs, where the outcome of interest was a reduction in thigh circumference.[2]

Typical use is in aesthetic clinics as an alternative to surgical liposuction or as a complement to diet and exercise for people near their goal weight; the abdominal study enrolled subjects with BMIs under 30.[1]

In the randomised comparison, 36 subjects were assigned to Vanquish ME or the original Vanquish; 34 completed, and the two who did not finished early for reasons unrelated to the study.[1] The primary outcome was abdominal fat thickness on ultrasound one month after the final session, and the Vanquish ME group showed a reduction of 4.17 mm, or 29.46 percent.[1]

A 2016 multi-centre randomised study in the Journal of Drugs in Dermatology compared Vanquish ME with its predecessor in 36 subjects and measured fat thickness by ultrasound.[1] A 2016 clinical trial in Dermatologic Therapy evaluated a selective RF applicator for reducing thigh circumference.[2] Both studies involved the manufacturer's platform, and follow-up in the abdominal study was one month after the last treatment.[1][2]

timeline.event: Clinical evaluations of the Vanquish ME abdominal protocol and a selective RF thigh applicator are published.[1][2]

card.summary: A hands-free radiofrequency device that heats fat to slim the abdomen and thighs over a short series of clinic sessions, with no contact or incisions.
card.note: Results measured in small manufacturer-linked studies; clinic pricing varies.

quick.overview:
Vanquish ME is a BTL Industries body-contouring machine that uses selective radiofrequency energy delivered without touching the skin.

It is used for the abdomen and thighs, usually as a series of weekly sessions in an aesthetic clinic.
quick.mechanism: Radiofrequency energy is aimed at the treatment area to warm subcutaneous fat selectively. In one study, abdominal fat thickness measured by ultrasound fell by an average of 4.17 mm after four weekly 45-minute treatments.
quick.risks: The published studies describe a non-invasive procedure with no incisions. Study sizes were small, and long-term outcomes were not reported in the sources found.
